fixture_note: FICTIONAL evaluation fixture for question generation; written by hand, no model calls.
plan: FICTIONAL EVALUATION FIXTURE. My team of four developers will deliver a customer portal for a client in eight weeks, using our existing authentication service. The client will provide the final design by the end of week two.

experts.objective: Technical risks of building the portal on the existing authentication service.
Whether the eight-week schedule holds given its dependencies.
questions: What matters most for timeline & dependencies?

experts.objective: Data-protection considerations for a customer-facing portal.
questions: What matters most for security & privacy?

findings.title: Client users may not exist in the authentication service
findings.observation: Depending on whether the client's users are already in the existing authentication service, a migration or new sign-up flow may be needed.
findings.why_it_matters: Unplanned migration work could consume a large part of the eight weeks.
assumptions: The client's users are not yet in the authentication service

findings.title: Acceptance criteria are not described
findings.observation: The plan does not say how the client will decide that the portal is complete.
findings.why_it_matters: Unclear acceptance can lead to late rework or disputes about scope.
assumptions: Acceptance criteria have not been agreed

assignment.objective: Technical risks of building the portal on the existing authentication service.

findings.title: A late design compresses build time
findings.observation: If the design arrives after week two, the remaining time for building and testing shrinks.
findings.why_it_matters: A compressed build raises the chance of missing the deadline or cutting testing.
assumptions: The build cannot start meaningfully without the final design

findings.title: Team availability across the eight weeks
findings.observation: Depending on whether the four developers also work on other projects, the effective capacity may be lower than four full-time people.
findings.why_it_matters: Lower capacity makes the eight-week deadline harder to meet.

assignment.objective: Whether the eight-week schedule holds given its dependencies.
questions: What matters most for timeline & dependencies?

findings.title: Personal data handling requirements
findings.observation: If the portal stores or displays customers' personal data, the client may have security or compliance requirements the plan does not mention.
findings.why_it_matters: Late-discovered requirements could add significant work.
assumptions: The portal will handle personal data

assignment.objective: Data-protection considerations for a customer-facing portal.
questions: What matters most for security & privacy?
